newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INSIGHT - DUTCH CHARTISTS SEE AEX LOSING MOMENTUM.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - DUTCH CHARTISTS SEE AEX LOSING MOMENTUM.

text.p: Dutch chartists see the start of a possible consolidation phase for the AEX share index as the recent march ahead continues to lose momentum.
However, longer term signals indicate the rally is not yet over, most believe.
The AEX index ended at 996.16 points on Friday, August 8, up 15.42 points on the previous Friday, but well back from Thursday's record close of 1010.97 points.

Note - Contributors' own analysis follows.

ING BARINGS - AEX chart is deteriorating as uptrend might be violated. Despite last week's new high at 1,010, prices are retracing recent gains after AEX's fall of 14 points in heavy volume towards 996.14, just above the former top at 996. This suggests uptrend is still intact.

However, the momentum chart is still making lower highs, indicating an uptrend running out of steam. A close below the support line, started in July around 860, and its nine-day moving average both around 988, would further delay positive scope and likely signal the start of a consolidation phase.

Strong money flow suggests no selling pressure yet, indicating downside potential should be limited. Also confirmed by solid market breath as the A/D ratio shows no weakness at all. A close below support level 988 would suggest another test of the horizontal 973 support area. A penetration of the solid horizontal 973 support level along with heavy volume would signal more downside towards horizontal support 956 or even lower towards the 930-920 support area.
All in all a close below support level 988 would violate the uptrend, indicating a likely test of the horizontal 973 support area. A possible consolidation phase should only be temporary.
Longer-term technicals remain solid.

MEESPIERSON - For the time being we stay neutral for our index. We see the Dow Jones leaning on its support levels. We think this support level will be strong enough. As we said last week, the dollar came down. At this level, around 2.08 (guilders) we see some support for the dollar.

RABO SECURITIES - Last week the AEX Index resumed the long-term uptrend by leaping the hurdle at 995. This break interrupted the short-term consolidation pattern. Despite this day's setback, there is still sufficient rooom for another surge.
A break at 1012 paves the way for another journey into uncharted territory. On the downside, the index is well-protected by the support at 957. Further south, support pops in at approximately 928.

GENERALE BANK - The outlook for the AEX on the very short term has changed somewhat after this Monday's break of the 985 level. This downard break makes us advise (investors) to remain NEUTRAL in the current market situation.
There is no clear direction to be detected for the index as long as it is caught between 995 and 975.
Outside the borders of this range a new direction will be chosen for the short term.

Below the 975 level, the trend which was initiated in the beginning of June comes in sight. As long as the current level of this trend (965) stays intact, there is no real danger of a major drop in prices. Below this intermediate support level 927 forms firm support in the long term. Above the 995 level a renewed attack on the previous tops becomes the most likely scenario.
Summarising, let the market choose a side before you act. Anticipation can be dangerous due to the volatile character of the market.
